body: admin/converge: a retired script path matches only where neither the character before nor the character after it is [A-Za-z0-9_.-]; the notes name the next character, and the previous-character guard keeps a profile-named path such as scripts/run-tag from matching inside myscripts/run-tag. The scan lists files with git grep -l -z -I -F (one -e per retired path) and finds the lines in Python with that pattern, rather than parsing git grep -n output.

admin/converge: the caller-issue filing and the intake import share one helper, intake_command(args, text), which runs ISSUES_SRC with OK_PLANNER_PROJECT_ROOT=root; import_issues calls it, and checks/owned-paths allows its subprocess.run in one intake_command region (replacing the import_issues region) rather than a second region for the filing. carried_intake and the new carried_review load through one carried_module(src); import_refusal takes the act it names ('the import' by default, 'issue <id>' for a filing).

admin/converge::workspaces_plan: the workspaces profile stays while port-block stays (the notes' rule) and also while a kept retired script outside the estate stays, since only the profile names that script and the next converge could not find its callers without it. A profile runTag.path or srcTag.path counts as a retired script only where it names a file inside the project root and outside .ok-planner/ (the old code would have offered to delete .ok-planner/bin/run-tag had the profile named it). A retired script that is itself a symbolic link goes to the estate-edits offer, as an uncommitted or linked-behind one does.

admin/converge::stale_wording_lines: a project.md line counts for the review-wording offer only where it still names .ok-review or .ok-plumbline/ once every retired script path is taken out, so the repoint alone owns script paths in project.md (I2, extended to .ok-plumbline/bin/plumbline and catalog-toc, which the old offer listed too) and diagnose never lists a line both as a repoint and as a review-wording offer. ADMINISTRATION's review-wording row and draft bullet say so.

admin/converge::write_owner opens its temp file with newline='' so every owner write, the repoint included, keeps line endings byte for byte; on POSIX this writes the same bytes as before. The repoint reads with newline='' (caller_text). migrate order: migrate_review, migrate_plumbline, migrate_callers (repoint, then file), migrate_workspaces, so a config the plumbline or review move brings into .ok-planner/ is repointed in the same run; plumbline_plan and workspaces_plan hold a script while a caller that gets an issue names it, computed from the scan, so the hold does not depend on whether the filing has run yet. A held script is neither removed nor offered.

admin/converge::caller_issue: each issue's title is '<file> names the retired <script> script'; its problem names the retired path(s), why converge leaves the line (the file's class, or the missing drop-in), whether the retired copy still stands, and lists each line as '- line N: <text>'; option A rewrites by hand (src-tag: to run-tag, one fresh tag per call; port-block: declare ports, then call .ok-planner/bin/port-block with the run's tag; otherwise to the suite's copy), option B keeps the retired copy (port-block: and the profile it reads), or, where no copy stands, deletes the lines. body: admin/converge: one predicate decides both the lint ignore repair and the review exclude rewrite (retired_entries/estate_state): an entry naming a retired estate goes once that estate is gone or its migration is unblocked (not blocked, and for .ok-workspaces/ no live worktrees waiting) and no kept retired script a caller still names sits inside it. The notes say 'once their estate is gone' for exclude; using the same predicate keeps one mechanism, lets diagnose report the exclude entries before converge migrates the estate, and differs from 'gone' only where leftover offers keep a migrated estate on disk. A repoint of a moved plumbline path (planner_path) needs only the migration unblocked, since a held script does not stop the moves.

admin/converge::retired_entries: an entry belongs to an estate when its first path segment, after a leading ./ or /, is .ok-plumbline, .ok-workspaces, or .ok-review, or is exactly .plumbline.json or .plumbline-budget.json; an entry naming a retired script with a drop-in is left to the caller repoint (one mechanism per job, as I1 rules); a repointed entry that the list already holds is dropped rather than duplicated. The lint config rewrite goes through swapped_text, so a repoint-only change keeps the file's formatting and a removal re-dumps it at the file's indent, as the review config rewrite already does.

admin/converge amend: the config path is accepted relative to the project root or as an absolute path naming one of the two files; a usage error is refused 'amend: it takes <config path> --from <draft>, ...; nothing written' exit 1 like every other refusal; an absent target is written new (so a project with no lint config can take a folders draft); amend refuses no uncommitted or linked target, since write_owner keeps a link and the owner accepted the whole draft, as the settings and config resolves do.

plugins/ok/skills/ok/SKILL.md and ADMINISTRATION.md: a report line (rules file, tracked CLAUDE.md, settings entry outside the wiring) counts as pending, like a declined draft or a core rewrite diagnose still reports; with any finding pending the /ok outcome reads 'converged; audit findings pending: <n>'. The audit's findings are written as 'audit: <file> — <finding>: <disposition>' with dispositions rewritten by converge, pending converge, written by amend, declined. A folder a sprint lists that config-check would refuse (outside the repository or not a directory) becomes a report line instead of a draft.
